settings.headline:
The load path,
proven before it's poured.
settings.copy: Keystone Structural designs the bones of buildings — steel, concrete, timber, and masonry — and proves every load path with analysis before a single foundation is poured.

trust_list.text: Full analysis: gravity, wind, seismic, and lateral

stats.label: Of projects delivered on the original schedule

settings.title: Analysis that
settings.intro: We don't guess at strength. Every member, connection, and foundation is sized by calculation and checked by a second engineer before it leaves our office.

features.title: Load-path clarity
features.text: We trace every load — dead, live, snow, wind, and seismic — from the roof down to the soil, so nothing is left to assumption and nothing is overbuilt.
features.detail: Every load traced roof to bedrock

features.title: Steel & connection design
features.text: From moment frames to trusses, we design steel members and their connections to be strong, simple, and economical to fabricate and erect.

features.title: Concrete & foundations
features.text: We size footings, slabs, and retaining walls against real soil reports, and design reinforced concrete that performs under both gravity and lateral forces.

features.title: Seismic & wind resilience
features.text: In high-seismic and high-wind regions we model the lateral system explicitly, so the building sways safely and stays upright when the ground moves.

features.title: Timber & masonry
features.text: We engineer wood-framed and masonry structures with the same rigor as steel — checking bearing, deflection, and fire-rated assemblies.

features.title: Construction support
features.text: Our engineers stay on the job through shoring, erection, and final inspection, answering RFIs and resolving field conditions before they become change orders.

settings.title: One firm,
settings.intro: Whatever your building is made of, Keystone has an engineer who has designed it before — and a second engineer who checked the math.

design.title: Structural steel frames
design.text: Moment frames, braced frames, and trusses for warehouses, offices, and industrial buildings — designed for strength and economy.

design.title: Connection design & detailing
design.text: Shop-ready connection details that fabricators can build without guesswork, reducing RFIs and erection delays.

build.title: Reinforced concrete
build.text: Footings, slabs, columns, and shear walls sized against real soil and load data, with clear rebar schedules for the field.

build.title: Foundations & retaining
build.text: Shallow and deep foundations, retaining walls, and below-grade waterproofing details that keep the structure stable and dry.

launch.title: Timber engineering
launch.text: Glulam, CLT, and light-frame wood systems engineered for bearing, deflection, and fire-rated performance.

launch.title: Masonry & hybrid
launch.text: Load-bearing masonry and mixed steel-timber-concrete systems, coordinated across trades for a buildable whole.

settings.title: From sketch to
settings.intro: A disciplined, documented path from first review to a sealed, buildable structure.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: We start with your drawings, the soil report, and the governing code. We flag the load paths and the questions that need answering before we model anything.

steps.title: Model
steps.text: We build a structural model of the building and run the full load cases — gravity, wind, seismic, and combinations — to see where the forces actually go.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: Members and connections are sized by calculation, then checked by a second engineer. We optimize for strength, cost, and buildability together.

steps.title: Document
steps.text: You get clear structural drawings, schedules, and a sealed calculation set that a contractor can build from and a reviewer can approve.

steps.title: Support
steps.text: We stay on site through shoring, erection, and final inspection — answering RFIs and resolving field conditions before they become change orders.

settings.note: Most of our work comes from contractors and architects who say the same thing: Keystone's drawings build clean, and the math is right the first time.

settings.title: Trusted with
settings.intro: Architects, contractors, and owners rely on our calculations to keep their projects safe, on schedule, and on budget.

settings.title: Straight answers,
settings.intro: The questions owners and architects ask us most before they engage a structural engineer.

items.question: When do I need a structural engineer?
items.answer: Any time a building is new, altered, or changing use — and often when you're adding a load like a rooftop unit or a mezzanine. If you're not sure, a quick review is cheap insurance.

items.question: Do you work with our architect or contractor?
items.answer: Yes. We coordinate directly with your architect and contractor, and we're used to being brought in at any stage — from early schematic to a field condition mid-construction.

items.question: What do your deliverables include?
items.answer: Structural drawings, member and connection schedules, a sealed calculation set, and construction-phase support. You get everything a contractor needs to build and a reviewer needs to approve.

items.question: How do you handle seismic and wind?
items.answer: We model the lateral system explicitly for your region's code requirements, so the building sways safely and stays upright under the design ground motion and wind load.

items.question: How are you different from a drafting service?
items.answer: A drafting service draws what you ask for. We engineer it — we size every member by calculation, check it with a second engineer, and seal it. The math is the product.

settings.title: Let's check your structure
settings.intro: Whether you're designing a new building or reviewing an existing one, we'd be glad to review your drawings and give you an honest read on the structural work required.
